title: Quant KV regen debug capsule
content:
Summary:
This capsule captures a short investigative sprint into a recurring correctness/regression pattern observed when serving quantized models with KV caching under microsampled long-context traffic. The bug appears as intermittent token-level corruption (wrong token predictions ~0.3–1.2% of requests) after KV-regen (cache rebuild) events triggered by guidance logic in the router. This doc is intentionally concise — notes, repro, quick experiments, and next actions.

Context / why we care:
- Customers running Dedicated and Private with compact 4-bit quant variants expect parity-level correctness for short/medium chats.
- We have automation that regenerates KV caches when model variant routing changes (e.g., swap to quantized variant). During regen we observed increased mismatch rate on the evaluation prompt suite used by onboarding tests.
- Impact: subtle accuracy regressions cause fallback rollouts and extra customer support churn.

Observed symptoms (field triage):
- Failure mode: token substitution (rare) and occasional partial repetition where sequence drifts after KV-regen boundary.
- Rate: ~0.6% during controlled synthetic replay (1M tokens), up to 1.2% in one production spike (regional).
- Correlation: spikes align with regen events within same second and with batch size changes (micro-batching from 1->8).
- Affected variants: post-training 4-bit quant (per-channel, asymmetric) more than 8-bit or fp16 baseline.

Lightweight repro (local):
1) Checkout runtime branch: reproduce/kv-regen-quant (local patch that toggles regen after model switch).
2) Start runtime with MODEL=compact-q4a, sequence-length=1024, batching=continuous, kv-shard=2.
3) Replay sample net traffic (scripts/repro/kv_regen_replay.py) containing 5k chat sessions with 6–12 token regen boundary events injected.
4) Observe token diffs against fp16 golden with difftool.
5) Outcome: token-diff rate ~0.5–0.9 vs baseline.

Experiments run (quick table):
- Exp A (baseline): fp16 no-regen. p-error: 0.00% (control).
- Exp B: q4a no-regen. p-error: 0.05% (tiny).
- Exp C: q4a regen synchronous. p-error: 0.62%. avg latency +3ms.
- Exp D: q4a regen async (deferred apply). p-error: 0.25%. avg latency +6ms.
- Exp E: q4a regen + deterministic-kv-serialize (new PR). p-error: 0.08%.
Notes: all p-error numbers are per-token substitution rate vs fp16 golden on the internal onboarding prompt set (2.4k tokens).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Floating-point -> quantized rounding nondeterminism during KV recomputation: arithmetic order and fused kernels produce slightly different keys. Small divergence accumulates on subsequent autoregressive steps. (High priority)
2) KV-shard boundary race: when regen occurs while a batch is in-flight, partial/old cache merges incorrectly (missing fence/atomic sequence). (Medium priority)
3) Microbatch padding interactions: different effective sequence lengths cause kernel path to choose a different attention optimization, changing numeric path. (Low/Medium)
4) Repo difference between quant kernels across devices (some kernels use int8 accumulate with small bias). (Exploratory)

What made hypothesis 1 more plausible:
- Re-running regen with deterministic-accumulation flag in the runtime cut p-error from 0.62% to 0.08% (Exp E).
- Diffing generated KV tensors before/after showed small elementwise deltas concentrated near the head-projection matrices.

Blockers & unknowns:
- We don't yet have a deterministic, low-overhead accumulation mode for all supported devices. Some customers can't tolerate the latency hit of fully deterministic kernels.
- Hard to reproduce at scale because the issue requires precise timing of regen vs in-flight micro-batches.
- Need additional long-sequence regression harnesses to validate on >10k token sequences without blowing compute budget.

Quick mitigations tested (and telemetry):
- Deferred apply (Exp D): buffer regen until in-flight batches complete. Effective but increased tail latency for first request (+6ms). Telemetry shows reduced p-error but not eliminated.
- Deterministic accumulate (Exp E): near-elimination of token mismatches in lab; latency overhead measured ~+2–5ms depending on device.
- Fallback policy tweak: on rollout, reduce microbatch size to 1 for 30s after regen (temporary). Tradeoff: lower throughput. We rolled this in as a quick mitigation under INF-703.

Proposed next actions (this sprint):
- Short term (by EOD Fri): add a lightweight deterministic-accumulate flag default=false but enabled for onboarding/regression runs. Owner: Ethan. Ticket: ML-2412.
- Mid term (1–2 weeks): implement an atomic fence around KV merge to prevent race at shard boundary + add unit harness to repro merges. Owner: Jonah. Ticket: INF-723 (subtask of INF-703).
- Mid term: add a microbenchmark suite (long-context streaming) to CI nightly that exercises regen timings at scale (approx 25k tokens per run). Owner: Priya. Linked: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/KB-1289.
- Long term: evaluate optimized deterministic kernels with vendor partners (NVIDIA/MLIS) for lower overhead; quantify perf vs correctness tradeoffs. Owner: Maya + SRE (Riley).

Action items (concrete):
- Ethan: push deterministic-accumulate flag PR and a short README on how to run onboarding with it (deadline: 2028-06-20).
- Jonah: prototype kv-merge-fence and produce a failing unit test that reproduces the race (deadline: 2028-06-25).
- Priya: build CI job stub and add to nightly (deadline: 2028-07-01).
- Riley (SRE): add a temporary rollout guard that lowers microbatch size after any variant swap for 60s (deadline: 2028-06-22).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could we snapshot and rehydrate KVs with CRC/hash checks to detect divergence early and fast-fail to fallback? Might be cheap and enable telemetry.
- Consider a hybrid approach: deterministic accumulate for head/key projection only (cheaper) + nondet for rest.
- We should capture a minimal token-level reproducible example and attach to ML-2412 for onboarding support to replay on customer environments.

Meeting minutes (quick):
- 2028-06-18 standup 10:05: reviewed Exp A–E; consensus: ship deterministic flag + fence prototype.
- Asked SRE to hold immediate rollouts in the region where spike seen until guard is in place.

Appendix: quick perf numbers (p99 tail, measured on 8xA10G):
- baseline fp16: p50 6ms / p99 18ms
- q4a no-regen: p50 5.5ms / p99 20ms
- q4a regen deterministic: p50 6.0ms / p99 21ms
- q4a regen async: p50 6.8ms / p99 26ms

If anything blocks you on the items above ping me on Slack (slack://user/Maya) or drop directly into ML-2412.

-- end capsule --
